source: YouTube auto-caption transcript 0:00-20:00 (tools/video_draft.py transcript re7j0kVSnUg --start 0 --end 1200), card names corrected against data/Sets/FRA_PremierDraft_All_Data.json; the transcript was read up to about 20:43, no content after about 20:00 is used. 'type' marks each idea as claim, heuristic or one-off pick; 'repeats' lists ideas of mqZsj4Vg2Es, CWsZxo1pB6Y and 994X9PlPInQ this one restates, 'related' same card or topic with a different claim.

ideas.claim: Hungering Puppetbeast is a good rare: a five-mana 5/5 that makes a Heartwood token on entering and can sacrifice an artifact for haste, trample or hexproof, so it protects itself and can start hasty.
ideas.quote: Protects itself when it comes down. Could be hasty when it comes down.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and ALSA of Hungering Puppetbeast against other rares; skill-split.

ideas.claim: Rewrite Regrets is a pushed reanimation spell in a set with landcyclers, and would be the second pick of P1p1 after the rare.
ideas.quote: anytime there's a reanimation spell in a set with land cyclers like these, I'm I'm all for it.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Rewrite Regrets by number of landcyclers / self-mill cards in the deck; pick position of Rewrite Regrets.

ideas.claim: Colour strength matters little for pick order: there will be stronger and weaker colours, but he drafts the cards that come, unlike in earlier sets where one colour was much better.
ideas.quote: I think there's going to be stronger colors and weaker colors in the set, but I don't think it should really affect your draft picks that much.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate by colour pair (GIH WR spread between pairs) against earlier sets; does colour-pair strength move the card win rates enough to matter?

ideas.claim: Bestial Incursion is better than Jiang Yanggu, Never Alone: it can be discarded or milled and has more synergy, while Jiang's untap of Heartwood tokens is cute.
ideas.quote: Beast Steel Incursion, honestly, I liked it more than Jong because ... you can discard it, you can mill it.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of the two cards; within-deck value with self-mill cards.

ideas.claim: Take the splashable removal spell (Memory Trap) over the card that wants to be cast early (Vigorbloom Charm): a splash card should be good whenever it is drawn.
ideas.quote: Memory trap's just like, you know, always going to be good no matter when you draw it.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of splash cards by turn drawn; Memory Trap vs Vigorbloom Charm GIH WR.

ideas.claim: In a green-red ramp deck the uncommon payoffs (Craftwork Crusher, Ruric Thar, Red Kiora) are what makes the archetype work, since a ramp deck usually has to rely on rares to have real top-end.
ideas.quote: to get enough like actual good ... expensive creature to ramp into, usually that means it's a rare, right? And so these existing at uncommon is just you know huge boon for these archetypes.
ideas.test_idea: Deck win rate of RG ramp decks by number of top-end payoffs; GIH WR of Craftwork Crusher and Ruric Thar by number of ramp cards.

ideas.claim: Compel Brutality is a good removal spell but easy to splash for a green deck, so it is not a high priority and is passed when other cards are better; he prefers to snipe the other cards.
ideas.quote: when I'm green, it's pretty easy to splash. And so I I don't take this one all that highly. I kind of like to snipe the other ones.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and ALSA of Compel Brutality; how often it is splashed (share of decks with off-colour Compel Brutality).

ideas.claim: Blue-white is one of the best decks in the format; Prudent Fateseer is one of the best cards for it and Campus Crier is good in blue and in any white deck.
ideas.quote: I really like blue white. Blue white's one of my favorite decks in the format.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate by colour pair, WU against the field; GIH WR of Prudent Fateseer.

ideas.claim: Take a landcycler over the splashable removal (Silence the Echo) when a white card is already a possible splash: the cycler fixes and the removal cannot be cast without the colour.
ideas.quote: I think it's a good point to take a land cycler here. We've already got like a white card that we want to splash potentially.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of Silence the Echo as a splash card; of splash decks by number of basic landcyclers.

ideas.claim: Card draw is valuable in ramp decks because it helps hit land drops and find ramp targets (Twinned Vision taken over the land).
ideas.quote: card draw is pretty nice in these ramp decks. You just want to be able to hit your lands, find your ramp targets.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Twinned Vision in decks with 4+ ramp cards against others.

ideas.claim: Dual lands are taken when nothing else is playable, but one with no use is a late pick (Innovative Commons): the blue-red land is fine, 'sure, why not'.
ideas.quote: Blue red land. Sure, why not. I don't think Cure is anything special.
ideas.test_idea: ALSA and win rate of Innovative Commons; taken position vs on-colour playables.

ideas.claim: Way of the Paradox over Arcane Amphisbaena in P2p1: it is cheap ramp, gains one life, and one life matters in slow decks, so the higher-upside card is taken; Amphisbaena is a close second.
ideas.quote: one life is the difference maker there. I think I'm going to take it here over ASB. That's close though.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Way of the Paradox vs Arcane Amphisbaena by deck speed; skill-split.

ideas.claim: A slow, ramp-based deck needs five, six or seven removal spells; a low, high-synergy deck (red-black, blue-white with synergies) can get by with fewer, but a deck that plans to go long must lock in removal.
ideas.quote: if you're a deck like this, planning to go long ... you just need to lock in a bunch of removal spells.
ideas.test_idea: Deck win rate of ramp decks by number of removal spells (0-3, 4-5, 6+), controlling for skill; same for synergy decks.

ideas.claim: Infinite Coursework is a worse card than Mindseeker Oculus, but he would take it over Oculus at that point because of the removal count.
ideas.quote: I think Oculus is a better card, but it's just like the removal.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Infinite Coursework and Mindseeker Oculus; removal-count interaction.

ideas.claim: Ferocity of the Hunt is a good enter-the-battlefield pair but does not suit big ramp decks: the card rots in the hand when you are trying to reach the mana for the giant, and it plays better with early creatures.
ideas.quote: if you have this card in your hand as you're about to cast this giant thing ... this card just is rotting in your hand, right?
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Ferocity of the Hunt by deck average mana value and ETB count.

ideas.claim: Apex Witchstalker is a strong ramp card for the graveyard, and a basic landcycler ('lock in some fixing') even before the splash colour has fixing, as long as the pack has fixing for it.
ideas.quote: putting stuff in the graveyard is generally good in this set. So, I'll lock in some fixing there.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of the Witchstalkers by deck colour, splash share; basic landcyclers as fixing.

ideas.claim: Most decks want only two tapped dual lands: even a multicolour deck will play them to cast spells, but they hurt tempo; he takes one because it fixes for the card he wants, accepting the cost.
ideas.quote: most decks only want two. Like if you're a two-color deck, you want two ... it does hurt you at some point.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate by number of enters-tapped dual lands in the deck (0, 1-2, 3-4, 5+); tapped lands in splash decks.

ideas.claim: With many strong cards in the format a double splash is acceptable for the best cards in the set because the set is slower and has a lot of fixing and card draw; normally he advises against splashing double-pip cards.
ideas.quote: I can stomach a double splash for some of the best cards in the set. Not always going to do it, but I think the tools are there.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of decks with a double-pip splash card by number of fixing sources; GIH WR of Chandra, Torch of Defiance.

ideas.claim: Chandra, Torch of Defiance draws cards, makes mana, kills things and ultimates in a few turns: strong enough to open and plan a double splash around.
ideas.quote: draws cards, makes mana, kills things. Uh, ultimates really quickly, right? Ultimates in just a few turns.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR and ALSA of Chandra, Torch of Defiance; skill-split.

ideas.claim: A land cycler that also fills the graveyard for Rewrite Regrets fulfils both roles, so it is taken over the black-green dual land.
ideas.quote: I think that fulfills our both roles there, right? It fixes us and it gets a card in the grave for rewrite regrets.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of Rewrite Regrets by number of landcyclers in the deck; ALSA of landcyclers.

ideas.claim: Take the removal spell over a good rare creature (Woodwork Prodigy) when the deck has little top end; with two or three more top-end threats he would take another ramp spell instead.
ideas.quote: I think I just take a removal spell here. ... If I have like maybe two more good top end threats, I just want to lock in another ramp spell.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Extended Absence against Woodwork Prodigy; effect of the pool's top-end count.

ideas.claim: A double-pip off-colour card (Hapatra, the Desert Fang with double black) is a stretch to splash but is still the best card in the pack; he hopes the fixing arrives.
ideas.quote: I'm just going to take Hapatra. Maybe we pick up enough fixing to make it work.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of Hapatra, the Desert Fang by number of black sources; splash share by pip count.

ideas.claim: Fixing land at the last second over playables: at pick five of pack three a red-white dual (Dedicated Commons) for a splash of Memory Trap is taken instead of a playable.
ideas.quote: I'm going to take the land.
ideas.test_idea: ALSA of Dedicated Commons; win rate of splash decks by number of fixing lands.

ideas.claim: Fblthp, Knows the Way fixes all colours: a legend that searches for basics by name, so it supports a multicolour splash.
ideas.quote: Fixes for all our colors.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Fblthp, Knows the Way by number of colours in the deck; as fixing: colours played vs sources.

ideas.claim: Take card quality when value is already enough: Archive Arbiter over a further card-draw spell because 'we're kind of good on value'.
ideas.quote: I think we're actually kind of good on value. I'll take Arbiter.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Archive Arbiter; pick-order effect of existing card draw in the pool.

ideas.claim: Filtering and card draw (Empower Jace cards, Something Worth Saving) help find the splash sources, so a mana base like this is more reasonable than the source count suggests.
ideas.quote: they can help you find your sources. So, they're not exactly fixing, but they make it a bit more reasonable, right, to have a mana base like this.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of splash cards with 0, 1-2, 3+ filter cards in the deck, controlling for sources.

ideas.claim: A black splash heavier than usual is justified when the deck lacks removal and fixing: 'just enough interaction'; red-green base splashing black and blue.
ideas.quote: one thing that's pushing me to play the black like a heavier black splash for this is we don't have all the fixing or all the removal in the world.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of RG decks splashing black by removal count in the splash colour.

ideas.claim: Cut the blue-black and blue-red tapped lands once red-green is the base: fewer tapped lands, and the cyclers do not have to fetch an Island.
ideas.quote: that makes me feel a lot more comfortable not having so many taplands and not having to play an island to go fetch with the cyclers.
ideas.test_idea: Effect of tapped lands on deck win rate in a splash deck; cyclers' basic type.

ideas.claim: Count sources including landcyclers and Fblthp: 11 green, 9 red, 10 black, then shave one Forest and one Swamp because the deck has too many lands.
ideas.quote: So we shave on a forest and shave on a swamp. I think that's probably the fix. It's still pretty good.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate by source counts per colour, counting landcyclers as sources; land count with landcyclers.

ideas.claim: This format punishes bad mana bases: you will have to do a mana base like this a decent amount of the time, and knowing the maths of an acceptable mana base is the most important thing to be a better limited player.
ideas.quote: this format's going to punish you or teach you because I think this is something you're going to want to do a decent amount of the time.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate against mana-base quality (sources per colour vs pips) in FRA decks.
